current_example.problem:
Given the function 
$f(\mathbf{x}; \mathbf{w}) = w_1x_1^{3} + w_2x_2^{3},$
compute $\nabla_{\mathbf{w}} \: f$ with the input ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217874/assets/cf91f8dff628ec86c154dddda69715801f187a51019584feba44942a0094abfa.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
To compute $\nabla_{\mathbf{w}} \: f$, we take partial derivatives with respect to each component of $\mathbf{w}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{w}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{w}_{1}}({w}_{1}{x}_{1}^{3}+{w}_{2}{x}_{2}^{3})={x}_{1}^{3} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{w}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{w}_{2}}({w}_{1}{x}_{1}^{3}+{w}_{2}{x}_{2}^{3})={x}_{2}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, with ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217874/assets/e74f207a7b6c74e9e63a5a61844e1b7340176402d8c9484afe61f08e8b861bcc.svg) we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{w}\,f & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{3} \\ {x}_{2}^{3}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}27 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
